residencyRequirements.description: The plaintiff must have been a resident of Idaho for a full six (6) weeks immediately preceding the filing of the complaint. There is no separate county residency requirement, but the complaint must be filed in the county where the defendant resides or, if the defendant is not a resident, in the county where the plaintiff resides.

waitingPeriod.description: A divorce cannot be granted until at least twenty-one (21) days after service of the summons and complaint on the defendant. Idaho Code §32-716.

noFault.name: Irreconcilable Differences
noFault.description: Irreconcilable differences have caused the irremediable breakdown of the marriage

fault.name: Habitual Intemperance
fault.description: Habitual intemperance (habitual drunkenness) of the defendant

fault.name: Conviction of a Felony
fault.description: Conviction of a felony by the defendant

fault.name: Permanent Insanity
fault.description: Permanent insanity of the defendant, established by competent medical testimony

separation.name: Living Separate and Apart for 5+ Years
separation.description: The spouses have been living separate and apart without cohabitation for a period of five (5) years or more

groundsForDissolution.notes: Idaho is both a fault and no-fault state. Approximately 99% of Idaho divorces are filed on the no-fault ground of irreconcilable differences. Fault grounds are available but rarely used.

propertyDivision.description: Idaho is a community property state. The court shall divide the community property substantially equally, unless there are compelling reasons to make an unequal division. The court must consider all relevant factors, including the duration of the marriage, any prenuptial agreement, the age, health, and earning capacity of each party, and the desirability of awarding the family home to the spouse with physical custody of children.
propertyDivision.separateProperty: Separate property (property acquired before marriage, by gift, or by inheritance) is confirmed to the spouse who owns it. Separate property is not subject to community property division unless commingled.

legalCitations.description: Division of community property — substantially equal

filingFees.notes: Idaho filing fees are approximately $207-$242 for a complaint for divorce depending on the county and whether children are involved. Fee waivers are available for qualifying low-income individuals via a Motion and Affidavit for Fee Waiver (Idaho Court Administrative Rule 9).

basic.description: Required information sheet filed with all family law cases

basic.name: Judgment and Decree of Divorce
basic.description: Final court order dissolving the marriage

service.name: Summons
service.description: Formal service on defendant via sheriff or process server

service.name: Acceptance of Service
service.notes: Must be signed by defendant and filed with the court

withChildren.description: Court order establishing custody and visitation schedule

withChildren.name: Child Support Worksheet
withChildren.description: Calculation per Idaho Child Support Guidelines (Idaho Code §32-706)

withChildren.name: Child Support Order
withChildren.description: Court order establishing child support obligations

formattingRequirements.notes: Per Idaho Rules of Civil Procedure

inState.description: Defendant must file a response within 21 days of service

outOfState.description: Defendant served outside Idaho must file a response within 21 days of service

responseDeadlines.statute: Idaho Rules of Civil Procedure, Rule 12(a)

childSupportGuidelines.description: Idaho uses an income shares model. Both parents' gross incomes are considered and the child support obligation is determined from the Idaho Child Support Guidelines schedule based on combined gross income and the number of children.
childSupportGuidelines.notes: The court may deviate from the guidelines upon a showing that application of the guidelines would be unjust or inappropriate. Factors include the best interests of the children and the financial resources of the parties.

maintenanceGuidelines.description: Idaho courts may award spousal maintenance where the spouse seeking maintenance: (a) lacks sufficient property to provide for reasonable needs, and (b) is unable to support themselves through appropriate employment or is the custodian of a child whose condition or circumstances make it appropriate not to require the parent to seek employment. The court considers the financial resources of the spouse seeking maintenance, the time necessary to acquire education or training, the duration of the marriage, the age and health of the spouse seeking maintenance, and the ability of the paying spouse to meet their own needs while paying maintenance.
maintenanceGuidelines.eligibility: Available at court discretion based on need and ability to pay. Idaho does not use a formula; the award is based on the totality of the circumstances.

court.name: District Court
court.description: Divorce actions are filed in the District Court in the county where the defendant resides, or if the defendant is not a resident of Idaho, in the county where the plaintiff resides.
